beats.intro: Derivatives, module seven. [[sub]]An interest rate swap is a series of forward exchanges at one fixed rate. This chapter prices swaps, and values them as time passes and rates change.
beats.series: [[a]]A forward rate agreement exchanges cash once. A swap exchanges cash every period. Both are firm commitments, with no money changing hands at the start, and both carry counterparty credit risk. [[fra]]A series of forward rate agreements would need a different fixed rate for each period: two point three nine six percent, four point four five three six, five point one seven one nine. [[swap]]A standard swap uses one fixed rate for every period. [[pt]]Some periods favor one side, some the other, but at the start the whole package has a value of zero. The swap rate is the internal rate of return on the implied forward rates.
beats.par: [[a]]To find the swap rate, set the present value of the fixed payments equal to the present value of the expected floating payments. The floating payments are expected to equal the implied forward rates. [[fl]]Discount each forward rate with the zero-rate discount factors. The three floating payments are worth eleven point one oh one seven percent today. [[df]]The three discount factors add up to two point eight oh oh five four five. [[res]]Dividing, the three-year swap rate is three point nine six four one percent. [[note]]It lies between the first forward rate and the last. A fixed-rate payer pays more than the floating rate in early periods, and less in later ones.
beats.esterr: [[a]]Why do issuers prefer swaps to forwards? Esterr has a floating-rate loan at the market reference rate plus one and a half percent. It pays a fixed rate of two point oh five percent in a swap, and receives the reference rate. [[s1]]Suppose the rate sets at three point seven five. Esterr receives one point seven zero on the swap, and pays five twenty-five on the loan. The net cost is three point five five percent. [[s2]]Suppose it sets at one point two five. Esterr pays point eight zero on the swap, and two seventy-five on the loan. The net cost is again three point five five percent. [[pt]]Whatever the rate, the interest expense is fixed: about two million two hundred eighteen thousand seven hundred fifty Canadian dollars a quarter.
beats.bond: [[a]]An interest rate swap behaves like a bond position. The fixed-rate payer is short a fixed-rate bond and long a floating-rate note. The principal amounts cancel, leaving only the coupons. [[recv]]So receiving fixed is like owning a fixed-rate bond. It loses when rates rise, and gains when rates fall. [[pay]]Paying fixed is like being short that bond. It gains when rates rise. [[use]]Swaps are liquid and have a benchmark exposure, so active managers use them to adjust interest rate exposure without buying or selling bonds. A manager who expects rates to fall can receive fixed.
beats.value: [[a]]After inception, the swap's value is the current settlement, plus the present value of all remaining settlements. [[ex]]Esterr pays two point oh five percent, while the expected floating rate starts at point five and climbs to three point seven eight. [[neg]]In early periods, the floating rate is below two point oh five, so Esterr pays a net amount. The first settlement is negative nine sixty-eight seven fifty. The second, negative eight eighteen seven fifty. [[pos]]From period eight, the floating rate is higher, and Esterr receives. [[mtm]]With the forward curve unchanged, time passing leaves the present value of remaining floating payments above the fixed ones. Esterr has a mark-to-market gain. [[up]]A rise in expected forward rates raises the floating side, and Esterr's gain grows. A fall would turn it into a loss.
beats.fyleton: [[a]]Fyleton is on the other side: a five-year receive-fixed swap on two hundred million pounds, at two point three eight percent against a floating rate of point seven one. [[s1]]The first settlement is one million six hundred seventy thousand pounds, in Fyleton's favor. [[time]]With an upward-sloping curve and no change in expectations, the present value of the floating payments it still owes exceeds the fixed it will receive. After settling, Fyleton has a mark-to-market loss. [[down]]If expected forward rates fall, the floating payments shrink, and Fyleton gains. [[bond]]This mirrors a fixed-rate bond: it trades at a discount as time passes on an upward curve, and at a premium when rates fall, while a floating-rate note stays at par.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]A swap is a series of forwards at one fixed rate, the par swap rate. [[w2]]The swap rate sets the present value of fixed payments equal to the present value of expected floating ones. [[w3]]Receiving fixed is like owning a bond, and paying fixed is like being short one. [[w4]]A swap's value is the current settlement plus the present value of what remains, and it moves with expected forward rates.
beats.finish: Module seven complete. Next: pricing and valuing options.
